intro.text: Mission Control, live. Forty-two thousand near-Earth asteroids on the board.
We taught a machine to decide which ones deserve worry.

act1.text: First, we gave the model everything.
It rediscovered NASA's exact rule for hazardous asteroids. Nobody told it.
Okay, that's actually kind of cool.

act2.text: Model B. We took away the answer key: no closest-approach distance.
It's working out the geometry from the shape of the orbit.

mistakes.text: Magenta: real hazards the model missed. Yellow: false alarms.
Every model does. Ours shows you where.

act4.text: Now the good part. NASA judges an asteroid's size by how bright it looks.
Unless it's dark. Our model went looking for big, dark rocks hiding in plain sight.

custom.text: Design your own asteroid. The model will judge it live.
Please don't make a big one.
